analysis: This batch contains only documentation changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md, lines 1-8) and a docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md update (date bump at line 3, 'Streaming read' row at line 65). No executable source is supplied. The docs say SSDBlockStore.readExactly now keeps a chunk or field in the buffer it was read into when one read returns it whole, instead of copying it into a second buffer. This reads as a memory and performance optimisation and does not change the DBK3 format, AES-GCM authentication, HMAC lookup tags, the TTL, or the no-follow IO and path-safety controls (T-041 mitigations). The docs say a chunk occupies one buffer instead of two while it is read, which slightly reduces plaintext-adjacent copies in process memory (T-014, TB-003). I found no regression and no new attack surface from the supplied text. The actual Swift diff (SSDBlockStore.swift, readExactly) is not in this batch, so I could not verify the following. Authentication must still complete before decrypted data is used. The retry raw-byte budget accounting must still hold (the doc row at line 278 cites readExactly). Partial reads must still be handled correctly, including the single-read fast path with short reads or EOF. Buffer reuse must not leak data across chunks. The code-level review of readExactly should be done in whichever pass receives that source file.
